answer: Each agent must lock a bond before it can act. A new identity is no cheap haven: the deposit costs real capital, so forging a thousand clones means staking a thousand deposits. Whenever the ledger reveals shared backing or copied behavior, slashing seizes the entire bond. This garden of costly commitments withers for fakers, while honest agents treat the bond as a lantern lighting the way to trust, since only real work earns it back.
